Hi Karen — following up with the technical evidence requested. Key points below; I'm attaching the subprocessor list and SOC2 summary.

1) Transfer mechanisms / legal basis:
- For our hosted Redwood API we support: (a) EU Standard Contractual Clauses (SCCs) executed as part of the DPA annex, and (b) EU-US Data Privacy Framework (DPF) self-certification details for customers electing cross-border flows to our US regions. 
- We document mapping per GDPR Articles 28/44/46 in the control matrix. See column "Legal Mechanism" in the attached matrix.

2) Subprocessors and locations:
- Attached redwood-subprocessor-list-20260425.csv — each row lists subprocessor, primary country, and function. We update this list weekly and provide a notification window per DPA.

3) Technical controls & keys:
- Encryption at rest with customer-key options: KMS-backed keys (Cloud KMS + optional HSM integration for Private deployments). We provide key rotation policies and can integrate with customer KMS via Dedicated/Private.
- TLS 1.2+ in transit; per-route tokenization options and prefix/KV caching described in matrix.

4) Logs & retention:
- Access logs retained 90 days by default for hosted; customizable for Dedicated/Private. Audit logs exported on request.

5) SOC2 & audit evidence:
- Attached redwood-soc2-summary-2025.pdf — summary of control families and contact to request full report under an NDA.

6) DPF specifics:
- We maintain a DPF self-assessment (available under NDA) and a public listing of our participation. For customers requiring only SCCs, we can default to SCCs in the DPA annex. For Novamed, if you prefer explicit DPF reliance please confirm and we will include DPF references in the annex.

Attachments: redwood-subprocessor-list-20260425.csv, redwood-soc2-summary-2025.pdf

If you want a redline window suggestion: we can commit to a 5-business-day turnaround for initial legal redlines after the annex is sent for signature.
